voice_units.voice: Ibn Abbas through Sa'id ibn Jubayr
voice_units.interpretation: Al-Kawthar is the good that God gave the Prophet; the river in Paradise is part of that good.
voice_units.arabic_locator: ثم قال البخاري حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم حدثنا هشيم أخبرنا أبو بشر عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس ... هو الخير الذي أعطاه الله إياه
voice_units.english_locator: al-Bukhari recorded from Sa'id bin Jubayr that Ibn Abbas said ... it is the good which Allah gave to him ... the river which is in Paradise is part of the goodness
voice_units.chain_fidelity: English preserves al-Bukhari, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ibn Abbas but omits Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, Hushaym and Abu Bishr.

voice_units.voice: Ibn Abbas through Sa'id ibn Jubayr
arabic_routes_as_printed: Abu Bishr AND Ata ibn al-Sa'ib
voice_units.arabic_locator: ورواه أيضا من حديث هشيم عن أبي بشر وعطاء بن السائب عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس ... وقال الثوري عن عطاء بن السائب عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
voice_units.english_locator: al-Bukhari also recorded from Sa'id bin Jubayr that Ibn Abbas said, Al-Kawthar is the abundant goodness
voice_units.chain_fidelity: The checked English preserves Ibn Abbas through Sa'id ibn Jubayr but does not preserve both printed Arabic route structures.

voice_units.interpretation: Al-Kawthar is abundant good in this world and the hereafter.
voice_units.arabic_locator: حتى قال مجاهد هو الخير الكثير في الدنيا والآخرة
voice_units.explicit_absence: The bounded English audit found no corresponding world-and-hereafter formulation.

voice_units.explicit_absence: No prophethood or Quran marker occurred in the bounded English cluster audit.

voice_units.interpretation: Al-Kawthar is a pool in Paradise.
voice_units.arabic_locator: وقال عطاء هو حوض في الجنة
voice_units.caution: The English uses 'pond' in a Prophetic report, but that does not establish translation of Ata's separate attribution.

shared_commentary_synthesis.statement: Ibn Kathir treats abundant good as broad enough to include the river and other gifts.
shared_commentary_synthesis.arabic_locator: وهذا التفسير يعم النهر وغيره لأن الكوثر من الكثرة وهو الخير الكثير ومن ذلك النهر
shared_commentary_synthesis.english_locator: This explanation includes the river and other things as well ... al-Kawthar linguistically means an abundance of goodness.

explicit_disagreements_or_scope_differen: River or pool language is narrower than the broad 'abundant good' explanation.
Mujahid explicitly spans this world and the hereafter.
Ikrima supplies a distinct triad: prophethood, Quran, and afterlife reward.
These are preserved as attributed alternatives or scopes, not harmonized into a single unanimous definition.
explicit_absences: No sentence-level English coverage is established for Mujahid's world-and-hereafter formulation.
No English coverage is established for Ikrima's prophethood, Quran, and afterlife-reward triad.
No English coverage is established for Ata's pool attribution as an Ata report.
No external source-edition locators or independent route comparisons have been completed.
